title: He Chose the Hereafter Over This World
subtitle: One scene changed the life of a young man from Quraysh forever.
heroQuote: «Saeed ibn Amir was a man who chose the Hereafter over this world and preferred Allah and His Messenger above everything else.»
intention: Read today's journey and reflect on how one sincere moment can change a person's life and lead them to choose the Hereafter over this world.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Saeed ibn Amir al-Jumahi was a young man from Quraysh, known among his people for his youth and strength. He lived in Makkah before Allah opened his heart to Islam. He did not realize that witnessing one event in Makkah would leave an impression on his heart that time could never erase. He witnessed the execution of the Companion Khubaib ibn Adi رضي الله عنه and saw his steadfastness and faith in the most difficult moments. That scene stayed with him until it became the beginning of his journey toward Islam. After embracing Islam, he migrated to Madinah and accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He later became an example of a just and ascetic governor who placed the pleasure of Allah above all the comforts of this world.

steps.title: A Scene That Changed a Life
steps.content:
Saeed ibn Amir went out with the people of Makkah to witness the execution of Khubaib ibn Adi رضي الله عنه. The people had gathered, and the leaders of Quraysh came forward, each wanting to see the end of a man who had remained steadfast in his faith. When Khubaib was brought to the place of execution, he asked them to let him pray two units of prayer. They allowed him to do so, and he prayed with humility and tranquility. Then he told them that if he did not fear that they would think he was prolonging the prayer out of fear of death, he would have made it even longer. After that, the polytheists began bargaining with him and asked him, «Would you love for Muhammad to be in your place while you were safe?» His answer was decisive. He declared that he would never accept even a thorn hurting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was safe among his family. He then prayed against those who had gathered to kill him and gave up his life with steadfastness and patience.

That scene never left Saeed's heart. Whenever he remembered that day, he would see Khubaib standing firm as he prayed, hear his words, and remember the certainty that had not been shaken by swords or threats. As the days passed, he realized that such steadfastness could only be the fruit of sincere faith, and that the man whom his companions loved so deeply must truly be a Messenger from Allah.

Allah opened Saeed's heart to Islam. He declared his faith without caring about what he might face from Quraysh. He then migrated to Madinah, stayed close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and witnessed with him whatever good and expeditions he was able to take part in.

After the death of the Prophet ﷺ, Saeed remained known for his honesty and asceticism. When Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه became caliph, he knew Saeed's position and trustworthiness and appointed him governor of Homs. The position did not change him. He continued to live a simple life, neither accumulating wealth nor seeking worldly comforts. He would spend whatever came to him on charitable causes and live modestly with his family.

Umar visited the people of Homs and asked them about their governor. They mentioned several things that puzzled him. They said that he did not come out to them early in the morning, did not receive people at night, was absent from them one day every month, and sometimes suffered fainting spells. When Umar asked Saeed about these matters, Saeed explained that he had no servant for his family, so he began his day by serving his household and preparing food before going out to the people. As for the night, he devoted it entirely to worshipping Allah. As for the day on which he was absent, it was because he washed his only garment and waited for it to dry. As for the fainting, it would return whenever he remembered the death of Khubaib and his tremendous steadfastness, overwhelming him with emotion until he lost consciousness.

Umar رضي الله عنه was delighted when he heard this and praised Allah that his good opinion of Saeed had been justified. He then sent him some money to help him, but Saeed did not see it as an opportunity to improve his lifestyle. Instead, he regarded it as a test that might distract him from the Hereafter. After consulting his wife, he distributed the money among poor Muslims and those in need, preferring what is with Allah over the comforts of this world, just as he had done since the day his life changed while witnessing the steadfastness of Khubaib رضي الله عنه.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Allah may make one sincere moment the cause of a person's guidance and completely transform the course of their life.
2. True faith becomes visible during hardship, as demonstrated by the steadfastness of Khubaib رضي الله عنه, which deeply affected Saeed.
3. Responsibility does not mean luxury. A position of authority can exist alongside asceticism, honesty, and service to others.
4. Whoever places the Hereafter before this world lives with a peaceful heart, and their good legacy remains among people even after they are gone.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: What situation do you know the truth about, yet continue to delay making a decision because you fear losing a worldly benefit or your standing among people?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Choose one good deed you can do today without expecting anything in return from people. Make your intention that it be sincerely for Allah, remembering that what is with Allah is better and more lasting.

title: The Messenger's Servant ﷺ
subtitle: A child given by his mother as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became one of the greatest narrators of his Sunnah.
heroQuote: «O Allah, grant him wealth and children, and bless him.»
intention: Read today's journey and reflect on how the companionship of righteous people, good upbringing, and mercy in dealing with others can shape a person who leaves a lasting legacy.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari was a young child whose heart was filled with love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before he had even seen him. His mother, al-Ghumaisa, planted faith in his heart and raised him to love the Prophet ﷺ, until he longed to meet him every day. He did not know that Allah would honor him with a companionship granted to very few people: he would spend ten full years serving the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, learning knowledge from him, witnessing his character, and carrying his Sunnah to generations after him.

steps.title: Ten Years in the School of Prophethood
steps.content:
Anas ibn Malik grew up in Yathrib. News of the Prophet ﷺ reached Madinah before his migration and filled people's hearts with longing for him. The young boy would hear this news from his mother, and his love for the Prophet ﷺ grew day after day until he longed to see him with his own eyes. When word spread among the people of Madinah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on his way, people would go out every morning waiting for his arrival. Anas would run with the other children toward the road, then return sadly when they did not find him.

Then the awaited day came. Madinah was filled with joy, and men and children went out to welcome the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while the women stood on the rooftops looking toward him and asking, «Which one is he?» It was one of the greatest days in Anas's life, and he remembered it even after he had passed one hundred years of age.

As soon as the Prophet ﷺ settled in Madinah, Anas's mother brought her son to him and said, «O Messenger of Allah... there is no man or woman among the Ansar who has not honored you with a gift, and I have nothing to offer you except this son of mine. So take him and let him serve you as you wish.» The Prophet ﷺ welcomed the boy warmly, placed his hand on his head, and embraced him, beginning a journey that would last ten full years.

Anas was ten years old. He grew up in the household of the Prophet ﷺ, observing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his worship, his dealings, his mercy, and his character. He memorized more of his words and actions than most others could. Those years became a complete school that shaped his personality, filled his heart with faith, and made him one of the Companions most knowledgeable about the life and characteristics of the Prophet ﷺ.

One of the greatest things Anas remembered was the beautiful character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said, «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was among the people with the finest character.» He narrated that the Prophet ﷺ once sent him on an errand, but Anas became distracted playing with children. He found the Prophet ﷺ standing behind him with a smile and saying gently, «O Unays, did you go where I told you to go?» Anas never heard a word of rebuke or saw anger. Instead, he saw a smile, teaching, and mercy. Years later he said, «By Allah, I served him for ten years, and he never said to me about something I had done, “Why did you do it?” nor about something I had left undone, “Why did you leave it?”».

The Prophet's care for Anas was not limited to kind treatment. He planted in his heart the values that build a person. He would address him gently as «my son», teach him not to go to sleep while carrying resentment toward anyone, encourage him to revive the Sunnah, and instruct him to spread greetings of peace among his family, explaining that this would bring blessing.

After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away, Anas lived for more than eighty years spreading the knowledge he had received and teaching people the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ. He became a reference for Muslims who turned to him whenever they encountered something they did not understand. Two days remained especially powerful in his memory: the day the Prophet ﷺ entered Madinah and the day he died. He would say that Madinah became illuminated when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, and when he died, everything in it became dark.

Allah answered the Prophet's supplication for Anas, blessing him with a long life, abundant wealth, and many descendants, until he saw more than one hundred of his children and grandchildren. Despite all these blessings, his heart remained attached to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He hoped to meet him on the Day of Resurrection and would say, «I hope to meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and say to him: O Messenger of Allah, here is your little servant, Unays.» When death came to him, he kept repeating, «There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,» until he met his Lord, after a life devoted to loyalty to the one who had raised and taught him.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Good upbringing begins at home. Anas's mother planted love for the Prophet ﷺ in his heart before he had even seen him.

2. Mercy and gentleness in teaching leave a greater impact than harshness, as demonstrated by the Prophet's treatment of Anas throughout his ten years of service.

3. Being close to righteous and virtuous people is a great blessing when a person makes good use of it for learning and action. Anas made the most of his companionship with the Prophet ﷺ until he became one of the major narrators of hadith.

4. True blessing is not merely abundant wealth or a long life. It is having these blessings become a means of spreading goodness and serving the religion of Allah.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: If you were in Anas's place and spent years beside a righteous role model, what quality would you hope to learn and make part of your daily life?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Follow the Prophet ﷺ in one character trait today. Choose to treat a child, a family member, or a colleague with kindness and patience, even if they make a mistake, and let mercy be your first response.

references: The Compilation of the Narrators of the Two Sahihs

title: The Seeker of Truth
subtitle: He left for Makkah as a leader among his people and returned as a believer carrying the light of guidance to his tribe.
heroQuote: «O Allah, grant him a sign that will help him accomplish the good he intends.»
intention: Read today's journey and reflect on how a fair-minded intellect and a sincere heart can lead a person to recognize the truth, remain steadfast upon it, and call others to it no matter how long the journey takes.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Al-Tufail ibn Amr al-Dawsi was the leader of the tribe of Daws and one of the noble Arabs known for generosity, chivalry, and sound judgment. He was an eloquent poet who could distinguish beautiful speech from ugly speech and judge matters wisely. He did not expect that an ordinary journey to Makkah would completely change his life, turning him into one of the great callers to Islam and eventually ending his life as a martyr for the sake of Allah.

steps.title: From Tribal Leadership to Leading Others to Guidance
steps.content:
Al-Tufail arrived in Makkah at a time when the confrontation between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Quraysh had reached its most intense point. As soon as he entered Makkah, the leaders of Quraysh surrounded him and warned him against meeting the Prophet ﷺ. They described his message in frightening terms, claiming that his words separated fathers from their sons and husbands from their families, until they convinced him not to listen to a single word from him.

Al-Tufail was so affected by what he heard that he put cotton in his ears when he went to the Sacred Mosque, fearing that he might hear something of the Prophet's words. But when he entered the mosque, he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ standing and praying near the Ka'bah. The sight and his devotion moved him, and Allah decreed that some of the Qur'an would reach his ears.

Al-Tufail said to himself: How can I allow myself to judge a man before hearing him? I am an intelligent man who knows good from evil. If what he says is good, I will accept it, and if it is otherwise, I will leave it. This decision became the beginning of the greatest transformation of his life.

He waited until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned home, then entered upon him and told him what Quraysh had done and how he had blocked his ears so that he would not hear his words. He then asked the Prophet ﷺ to present Islam to him. The Prophet ﷺ recited Surah al-Ikhlas and Surah al-Falaq to him. Al-Tufail found in the beauty of the Qur'an and the justice of Islam something he had never heard before, so he extended his hand, testified to the two testimonies of faith, and embraced Islam with conviction and certainty.

He remained in Makkah for a period, learning Islam and memorizing whatever portions of the Qur'an he could. Then he asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to return to his people and call them to Islam. He explained that he was obeyed among them and asked Allah to grant him a sign that would help him in this mission. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for him. Allah answered the supplication, and a light appeared between his eyes. Fearing that his people would think it was a punishment for his conversion, he asked Allah to move it elsewhere. The light was then transferred to the top of his whip, so people could see it like a glowing lamp.

He began his call with those closest to him. When his father came, he told him about his Islam. His father accepted, purified himself, and learned Islam. His wife also accepted the call after he explained to her the truth of monotheism and the falsehood of worshipping idols.

As for the tribe of Daws, they did not respond quickly. Abu Hurairah رضي الله عنه was among the first of them to embrace Islam. Al-Tufail continued calling his people, but their response was slow. He returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him what he had encountered. Some of the Companions thought the Prophet ﷺ might pray against them, but he raised his hands and said, «O Allah, guide Daws... O Allah, guide Daws... O Allah, guide Daws.» He then instructed Al-Tufail to return to his people, treat them gently, and continue calling them.

Al-Tufail obeyed the Prophet's command. He did not despair, become angry, or abandon the call because of the slow results. He remained among his people for years, calling them with wisdom and patience, until the Prophet ﷺ migrated to Madinah and the battles of Badr, Uhud, and the Trench took place. Al-Tufail then came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with eighty households from Daws who had embraced Islam and become devoted Muslims. The Prophet ﷺ was delighted with them and honored them.

After the conquest of Makkah, Al-Tufail asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to destroy his people's idol, Dhu al-Kaffayn. He was given permission. He went to it publicly while his people waited for punishment to descend upon him from the idol. Instead, he set it on fire while reciting his famous verses. The idol burned, and with it disappeared the last remnants of polytheism among the tribe of Daws, whose people then entered Islam.

After the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Al-Tufail remained firm upon his commitment. He participated with the Muslims in fighting the apostates during the caliphate of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه. On his way to the Battle of Yamamah, he saw a dream and interpreted it as glad tidings of martyrdom, and that his son Amr would later follow him on the same path.

At the Battle of Yamamah, Al-Tufail fought bravely until he was martyred, just as he had hoped. His son Amr was severely wounded and lost his hand, but he lived until he eventually attained martyrdom at the Battle of Yarmouk. Thus Al-Tufail was a martyr and the father of a martyr.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. A person should not judge the truth based solely on what others say. They should investigate for themselves and be fair before reaching a conclusion.

2. A successful caller to truth begins with those closest to him and combines wisdom, gentleness, and patience no matter how delayed the results may be.

3. Success in calling others to Islam is not measured by how quickly people respond. Al-Tufail remained patient for years until his call bore fruit through the acceptance of his people.

4. Whoever is sincere in seeking the truth and remaining steadfast upon it, Allah grants them a good ending. Al-Tufail's life ended with martyrdom after a lifetime spent serving Islam.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: Have you ever formed an opinion about a person or an idea based on what people said without seeking the truth for yourself? How can Al-Tufail be a role model for fairness and sincere inquiry?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Choose a person or subject you have already judged, and try today to approach it fairly. Seek the truth from its source before forming a final judgment.

title: He Would Not Sell His Faith
subtitle: He stood as a prisoner before one of the greatest kings of his age and found nothing in the entire world worth trading for his faith.
heroQuote: «It is the right of every Muslim to kiss the head of Abdullah ibn Hudhafa, and I shall be the first to do so.»
intention: Read today's journey and reflect on how faith keeps a person steadfast when the entire world is offered to them in exchange for giving up their religion.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Abdullah ibn Hudhafa al-Sahmi was a Companion whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ chose to carry his letter to Khosrow, the King of Persia, in the sixth year after the Hijrah. He was entrusted with one of the great missions that required courage and steadfastness: carrying the Prophet's letter to a powerful king in a distant land whose people, language, and royal customs he did not know. Allah later decreed that Abdullah would meet Caesar, the Byzantine emperor, in another story in which he demonstrated remarkable steadfastness in the face of threats and temptation, becoming an example of a man who would never bargain away his faith regardless of the price.

steps.title: A Faith That Could Not Be Bargained Away
steps.content:
In the sixth year after the Hijrah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ decided to send several of his Companions with letters to the kings of Arabia and foreign lands, inviting them to Islam. It was a highly dangerous mission. These messengers would travel to distant countries and meet kings whose personalities they knew nothing about, inviting them to abandon their religions and authority and enter Islam.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered his Companions and addressed them, telling them that he wanted to send some of them to the foreign kings. His Companions responded that they would carry out whatever he wanted and go wherever he wished.

The Prophet ﷺ chose six of his Companions to carry his letters to the kings, and Abdullah ibn Hudhafa al-Sahmi was one of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ chose him to carry his letter to Khosrow, the King of Persia.

Abdullah prepared his mount, said farewell to his wife and child, and set out alone on the long journey, carrying nothing but his reliance upon Allah. He eventually reached Persia, requested permission to enter the king's presence, and informed the royal court that he was carrying a letter.

Khosrow ordered his palace to be decorated and summoned the nobles of Persia to his gathering. He then allowed Abdullah to enter. Abdullah entered in simple clothing, but he held his head high and stood firmly, carrying in his heart the dignity of Islam and the pride of faith.

Khosrow gestured to one of his men to take the letter from Abdullah's hand, but Abdullah refused. He said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded him to deliver the letter directly to Khosrow and that he would not disobey the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Khosrow allowed him to approach, so Abdullah stepped forward and handed him the letter himself.

Khosrow summoned an Arab scribe from al-Hirah to read the letter. It began: «In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Khosrow, the great king of Persia. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance.»

As soon as Khosrow heard the beginning of the letter, he became extremely angry because he could not accept that the letter began with the name of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before his own name. He took the letter, tore it apart, and ordered Abdullah to be removed from the gathering.

Abdullah left Khosrow's court not knowing what would happen to him. Would he be killed or allowed to leave freely? But he did not allow fear to shake his heart. He said, «By Allah, I do not care what happens to me after I have delivered the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.» Then he mounted his ride and departed.

When Khosrow's anger subsided, he ordered Abdullah to be brought back, but Abdullah was nowhere to be found. He had already begun his journey home. When Abdullah reached the Prophet ﷺ, he told him what had happened, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, «May Allah tear apart his kingdom.»

Khosrow then wrote to his governor in Yemen, ordering him to send two strong men to capture the Prophet ﷺ and bring him to Khosrow. Badhan sent two of his best men and instructed them to investigate the Prophet ﷺ and return with news.

The two men arrived in Madinah and informed the Prophet ﷺ that Khosrow had ordered Badhan to send people to bring him to the king. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ told them to return to him the following day.

The next day, the Prophet ﷺ told them that Khosrow had been killed and that Allah had given authority over him to his son Shirawayh that very night. He instructed them to tell Badhan that the Prophet's religion would reach as far as Khosrow's kingdom had reached, and that if Badhan embraced Islam, the Prophet ﷺ would leave him in control of his authority and kingdom over his people.

The two men returned to Badhan and told him what the Prophet ﷺ had said. Soon afterward, a letter arrived from Shirawayh informing Badhan that he had killed Khosrow. At that point, Badhan realized that what Muhammad ﷺ had told them had occurred exactly as he had said. He declared his Islam, and the Persians living in Yemen embraced Islam along with him.

But Abdullah ibn Hudhafa's encounters with kings did not end there.

In the nineteenth year after the Hijrah, Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه sent an army to fight the Byzantines, and Abdullah ibn Hudhafa was among them. Caesar, the Byzantine emperor, had heard about the faith of the Muslims, their steadfastness, and their willingness to sacrifice themselves for the sake of Allah. He ordered his men that if they captured any Muslim, they should bring him alive to him.

Allah decreed that Abdullah would fall captive into Byzantine hands. They took him to their king. Caesar looked at him for a long time and then offered him the chance to become a Christian, promising that if he did so, he would release and honor him.

Abdullah firmly rejected the offer and declared that death was more beloved to him than abandoning his religion. Caesar tried to tempt him further, offering to share his kingdom and authority with him, but Abdullah refused again, confirming that he could never abandon the religion of Muhammad ﷺ even if he were given the entire world.

Caesar realized that neither wealth nor authority could move Abdullah from his faith, so he intensified his threats. Yet Abdullah remained steadfast, refusing to bargain over his beliefs or allow fear to change his position.

Caesar then moved to an even harsher test, attempting to force Abdullah to abandon his religion. Despite the severity of the situation, Abdullah remained firmly attached to his faith until Caesar finally gave up hope of making him retreat.

At another point, Caesar offered Abdullah a proposal that would secure his freedom and also result in the release of Muslim prisoners in exchange for Abdullah kissing his head. Abdullah saw that accepting this did not mean abandoning his religion and would lead to the rescue of himself and the Muslim prisoners, so he accepted and kissed Caesar's head. The king then ordered the prisoners to be released and handed over to Abdullah.

Abdullah returned to Madinah and told Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه what had happened. Umar was extremely happy. He then looked at the prisoners and said, «It is the right of every Muslim to kiss the head of Abdullah ibn Hudhafa, and I shall be the first to do so.» Umar then stood and kissed Abdullah's head.

Thus Abdullah left his encounters with kings exactly as he had entered them: steadfast in his faith, neither tempted by worldly wealth, frightened by royal power, nor driven by fear to surrender what he believed.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. True faith becomes visible when remaining steadfast upon one's principles becomes costly. Abdullah ibn Hudhafa did not allow threats or temptation to make him abandon his religion.

2. A person's strength is not found in their status or wealth but in their certainty in Allah. Abdullah stood before mighty kings carrying the dignity of Islam in his heart.

3. Wisdom does not mean surrendering one's principles. Abdullah refused to abandon his religion, yet accepted an action that would lead to the release of Muslim prisoners without compromising his faith.

4. A steadfast موقف can leave an impact far beyond the person who takes it. Abdullah returned from captivity, and his steadfastness became a reason for freeing Muslim prisoners and a remarkable event preserved by history.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: If you were offered comfort, money, or status today in exchange for giving up a principle you believe in, what would help you remain steadfast?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Identify one religious principle you want to remain steadfast upon today, then commit to it in one practical situation even if nobody notices. Make your steadfastness solely for Allah.

references: The Prophetic Biography by Ibn Hisham, edited by al-Saqqa
The Lives of the Companions by Muhammad Yusuf Kandhalawi, Volume 4

title: From Enemy to Brother
subtitle: He went to Madinah intending to kill the Prophet ﷺ, but returned to Makkah calling his people to Islam.
heroQuote: «By Allah, Umayr ibn Wahb has become more beloved to me than some of my own sons.»
intention: Read today's journey and reflect on how guidance can transform a person's heart from hostility to love, and from fighting the truth to calling others toward it.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Umayr ibn Wahb al-Jumahi was one of the men of Quraysh. He returned from Badr having survived, while his son Wahb remained a prisoner in the hands of the Muslims. Umayr feared for his son and carried deep hatred toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because of what he thought of his call to Islam. But Allah led him to Madinah in a story that began with the intention of killing the Prophet ﷺ and ended with Umayr embracing Islam and becoming one of the callers to Allah in Makkah.

steps.title: When the Heart Changed
steps.content:
After the Battle of Badr, Umayr ibn Wahb was living with the pain of defeat, while his son Wahb was among the prisoners in Muslim hands. One day, Umayr went to the Sacred Mosque and found Safwan ibn Umayyah sitting beside the Hijr. The two men sat talking about Badr, the Quraysh who had been killed, and the prisoners they had lost.

Safwan said, «By Allah, there is no good in life after them.» Umayr agreed, then mentioned what prevented him from going to Madinah to kill Muhammad ﷺ: debts he had no means of paying and a family he feared would be left without support after him. He also pointed out that his son Wahb being a prisoner among the Muslims would make his journey to Yathrib seem natural and would not raise suspicion.

Safwan seized the opportunity and promised to take care of all of Umayr's debts and provide for his family as if they were his own. They agreed to keep their conversation secret, and Umayr left having resolved to carry out their plan.

Umayr ordered his sword to be sharpened and poisoned, then mounted his ride and headed toward Madinah, carrying hatred and the intention he had resolved upon in his heart.

In Madinah, Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه was sitting with some of the Companions near the door of the mosque, remembering Badr and the prisoners and dead it had left behind. Suddenly, Umar saw Umayr ibn Wahb approaching the mosque with his sword. Umar knew that he had not come with good intentions. He hurried to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him. The Prophet ﷺ ordered him to bring Umayr in.

Umar took Umayr to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ told Umar to release him and keep away from him. He then invited Umayr to come closer and began speaking with him.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him why he had come. Umayr said that he had come because of the ransom for his imprisoned son. The Prophet ﷺ then asked him about the sword he was carrying. Umayr tried to conceal the truth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, «Tell me the truth, Umayr. What have you come for?»

The Prophet ﷺ then told him about the conversation he had had with Safwan ibn Umayyah beside the Hijr: they had remembered the Quraysh killed at Badr, and Umayr had said that if it were not for his debts and family, he would go and kill Muhammad ﷺ. Safwan had agreed to take care of his debts and family in exchange, but Allah had prevented Umayr from carrying out what he intended.

Umayr was stunned. This was a conversation known only to him and Safwan. No one else knew what they had agreed upon. At that moment, he realized that the Prophet ﷺ could only have known this through revelation from Allah.

Umayr said, «I testify that you are the Messenger of Allah.» He admitted that he and his people had accused the Prophet ﷺ of lying about the news he received from heaven, but he now knew that what the Prophet ﷺ had told him about his private conversation with Safwan could only have come from Allah. He praised Allah for bringing him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he could be guided to Islam.

Umayr testified that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and he embraced Islam.

The Muslims were overjoyed at his conversion. Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه said, «A pig was more beloved to me than Umayr ibn Wahb when he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but today he is more beloved to me than some of my own sons.»

Umayr began learning Islam and filling his heart with the light of the Qur'an. He lived a new life that made him forget what he had been before. After learning what he could of his religion, he came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked permission to return to Makkah—not to harm the Muslims as he once had, but to call Quraysh to Allah and His Messenger.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him permission. Umayr returned to Makkah and went to Safwan ibn Umayyah. He spoke to him as one of Quraysh's leaders and intelligent men, asking how worshipping stones and sacrificing to them could be a religion that agreed with reason. He then publicly declared, «I testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.»

Umayr began calling people to Allah in Makkah, and many people embraced Islam through him. Thus his life was transformed from that of a man who carried a sword and hatred into that of a man who carried faith and a message, and from an enemy of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into a brother loved by the Muslims. He eventually became one of the people most beloved to Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. We should never despair of someone's guidance because of their past. Even the strongest opponent can become a supporter of the truth when Allah opens their heart.

2. Being honest with oneself and facing the truth can become the beginning of repentance. When Umayr realized that the Prophet ﷺ knew what he had hidden, he did not persist in his stubbornness. Instead, he acknowledged the truth and embraced Islam.

3. True repentance is not limited to abandoning a mistake; it becomes righteous action. Umayr moved from fighting Islam to calling people toward it.

4. People's love and trust can change when a person's actions change. After embracing Islam, Umayr became beloved by the Companions after having once been among their fiercest opponents.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: Is there a past mistake or situation that makes you think change has become difficult, even though the story of Umayr ibn Wahb reminds you that a person can begin a new life?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Take one sincere step today toward fixing something you know you need to change, then turn that change into a righteous action that continues beyond today.

references: The Lives of the Companions: Indexes in Volume 4
The Prophetic Biography by Ibn Hisham, edited by al-Saqqa

title: The Brave One Who Never Retreats
subtitle: He was thin in body, but his heart was firmer than mountains on the battlefields.
heroQuote: «O people of the Ansar, let none of you think of returning to Madinah. There is no Madinah for you after today. It is only Allah, and then Paradise.»
intention: Read today's journey and reflect on how faith and courage can drive a person to remain steadfast when trials become severe.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Al-Bara ibn Malik al-Ansari was the brother of Anas ibn Malik, the servant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Bara did not have a strong physique or an imposing appearance. He was described in the source as disheveled, dusty, thin, and with little flesh on his body. Yet this apparently weak body carried a heart of extraordinary courage and boldness. Al-Bara became known for his fearlessness in battles, to the point that Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه wrote to his governors instructing them not to appoint him commander of a Muslim army, fearing that his boldness might expose his soldiers to danger.

steps.title: A Heart That Knew No Retreat
steps.content:
Al-Bara's story began during one of the most difficult periods in Islamic history, after the death of the Prophet ﷺ, when many Arab tribes abandoned Islam. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه stood against this turmoil. He prepared eleven armies of Muhajirun and Ansar and sent them throughout the Arabian Peninsula to confront the apostates and return people to the path of Islam.

Among the strongest of these apostates were Banu Hanifah, the followers of Musaylimah the Liar. Musaylimah gathered a large number of fighters, many of whom followed him out of tribal loyalty rather than conviction in his message.

The Muslims first confronted Musaylimah with an army led by Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, but he was unable to bring the battle to a decisive conclusion. Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه then sent another army under the command of Khalid ibn al-Walid, and among its ranks were several senior Companions, including Al-Bara ibn Malik.

The two armies met at Yamamah. At the beginning of the battle, the advantage shifted toward Musaylimah's followers. The Muslim ranks became unsettled until his followers managed to reach Khalid ibn al-Walid's tent. Khalid then reorganized the army and gave each group of Muslims its own banner so that the performance of each group could be identified and the Muslims could recognize where the weaknesses were.

The battle intensified, and the Muslims displayed tremendous steadfastness. Several Companions demonstrated great courage that day, including Thabit ibn Qays, Zayd ibn al-Khattab, and Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah. The source, however, highlights Al-Bara ibn Malik's role as one of the most remarkable moments of the day.

When the fighting intensified, Khalid ibn al-Walid turned to Al-Bara and said, «To them, young man of the Ansar!» Al-Bara then turned to his people and said, «O people of the Ansar, let none of you think of returning to Madinah. There is no Madinah for you after today. It is only Allah, and then Paradise.»

Al-Bara and those with him then charged toward the polytheists and broke through their ranks until Musaylimah's followers were forced to retreat and seek refuge inside a large garden that later became known as the Garden of Death because of the large number of people killed there that day.

The garden had high walls, and Musaylimah's followers closed its gates and fortified themselves inside. They began throwing weapons at the Muslims from above the walls. At that point, Al-Bara proposed an extremely bold plan. He said to his people, «Put me on a shield, raise the shield on spears, then throw me into the garden near its gate. Either I will be martyred, or I will open the gate for you.»

Al-Bara was carried on the shield and thrown into the garden. He managed to reach its gate and open it despite suffering many wounds. The Muslims entered through the gates and over the walls, and the fighting intensified until they reached Musaylimah and killed him, bringing the battle to an end with a Muslim victory.

Al-Bara was then taken to his quarters for treatment. Khalid ibn al-Walid remained with him for a period, treating his wounds until Allah granted him recovery.

But Al-Bara did not stop seeking martyrdom. He continued longing for the aspiration that had not been fulfilled for him at Yamamah and continued participating in battles, hoping to meet Allah.

Then came the day of the conquest of Tustar in Persia. The Persians had fortified themselves inside a powerful fortress. The siege grew long and the hardship intensified. During the fighting, one of the grappling hooks thrown by the defenders from above the fortress caught his brother Anas ibn Malik. When Al-Bara saw his brother, he rushed to save him and managed to reach and rescue him despite the severity of the situation.

During that battle, Al-Bara ibn Malik prayed to Allah to grant him martyrdom. Allah answered his supplication, and he fell as a martyr after a life filled with courage, boldness, and longing to meet Allah.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. A person's value is not measured by their appearance or physical strength. Al-Bara was thin in body, yet he became known for courage and steadfastness.

2. True courage does not mean reckless action. It means remaining firm in danger and being willing to take responsibility during the most difficult moments.

3. Faith can give a person an inner strength that keeps them steady when the ranks around them are shaken.

4. Al-Bara carried a sincere longing to meet Allah, so he continued seeking martyrdom until he attained it in the battle in which he prayed for Allah to grant it to him.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: When you face a difficult situation today, do you allow fear to push you toward retreat, or can you remain firm and do what is right with wisdom and courage?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Choose one situation in which you hesitate because of fear. Today, take one correct and well-considered step toward facing it instead of running away from it.

references: The Prophetic Biography by Ibn Hisham
The Lives of the Companions, Volume 4
Leaders of the Conquest of Persia by Shayt Khattab
